**Proposed mechanism:** UMOD (HGNC:12425) —DISRUPTS→ Protein homeostasis and quality control (GO:0031984); Protein homeostasis and quality control (GO:0031984) —LEADS_TO→ Familial juvenile hyperuricemic nephropathy (MONDO:0008073); STT3A (HGNC:11029) —DISRUPTS→ N-glycosylation (GO:0006486); N-glycosylation (GO:0006486) —LEADS_TO→ Protein homeostasis and quality control (GO:0031984); Protein homeostasis and quality control (GO:0031984) —LEADS_TO→ STT3A-congenital disorder of glycosylation (MONDO:0014270). Loss-of-function mutations in UMOD lead to impaired protein homeostasis and cellular dysfunction in renal cells, manifesting as FJHN1. Concurrently, loss-of-function mutations in STT3A disrupt N-glycosylation, a critical pathway impacting overall protein homeostasis and quality control, leading to STT3A-CDG. The convergence occurs at the level of cellular protein homeostasis and quality control pathways, which are compromised by defects in both UMOD processing/secretion and N-glycosylation.

**How to falsify it:** Demonstration that mutations in UMOD do not lead to any detectable alteration in protein processing, folding, or trafficking pathways, or that STT3A function is entirely independent of these general cellular quality control mechanisms. _(variant: Any common variant (AF > 0.01) in STT3A or UMOD associated with either disease phenotype.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the overlap in cellular protein homeostasis pathways affected by distinct genetic defects in FJHN1 and STT3A-CDG could reveal common therapeutic strategies targeting protein quality control, chaperone function, or endoplasmic reticulum-associated degradation (ERAD) pathways that might benefit patients with either condition.

#### 2. X-linked immunodeficiency with magnesium defect, Epstein-Barr virus infection and neoplasia  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.379)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-446203)

**Proposed mechanism:** UMOD (HGNC:12162) —DISRUPTS→ Urea cycle (REACT:R-HSA-680971); Urea cycle (REACT:R-HSA-680971) —DECREASES→ Urea (CHEBI:17792); Urea (CHEBI:17792) —LEADS_TO→ Hyperuricemia (HP:0002152); Hyperuricemia (HP:0002152) —LEADS_TO→ Renal dysfunction (HP:0000119); MAGT1 (HGNC:14744) —DISRUPTS→ Magnesium homeostasis (GO:0006798); Magnesium homeostasis (GO:0006798) —DECREASES→ Magnesium ion (CHEBI:27036); Magnesium ion (CHEBI:27036) —LEADS_TO→ Immunodeficiency (HP:0002711); Immunodeficiency (HP:0002711) —LEADS_TO→ Neoplasia (HP:0002664). Loss-of-function mutations in UMOD disrupt the urea cycle, leading to urea accumulation and subsequent hyperuricemia and renal dysfunction in FJHN1. Similarly, loss-of-function mutations in MAGT1 disrupt magnesium homeostasis, causing magnesium deficiency and leading to immunodeficiency and increased risk of neoplasia in XMEN. The convergence lies in the disruption of essential metabolic/homeostatic pathways (urea cycle and magnesium homeostasis) leading to distinct but severe pathological outcomes.

**How to falsify it:** Demonstration that mutations in UMOD do not impair urea cycle function or lead to hyperuricemia, or that mutations in MAGT1 do not affect magnesium levels or immune function. _(variant: Exome sequencing data from gnomAD showing a pathogenic variant in UMOD or MAGT1 with a minor allele frequency above 0.1% in the general population would challenge the rarity and pathogenicity of the proposed causal variants.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the distinct impacts of disrupting the urea cycle versus magnesium homeostasis can inform targeted therapeutic strategies. For FJHN1, interventions aimed at managing uric acid levels are relevant. For XMEN, magnesium supplementation and immune support are crucial, and exploring therapies to mitigate neoplasia risk is important. Identifying these distinct pathway disruptions highlights the need for personalized medicine approaches based on the specific molecular defect.
